anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer selects or reuses a substantially sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are accurate, inflating execution cost and runtime footprint.
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent transactions contend for incompatible locks, generating long blocking chains or deadlocks that stall throughput.
Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly : The database process hits kernel-enforced limits on objects such as file handles, processes/threads, or shared-memory segments, preventing further resource allocation.

When all three root causes coexist, the workload may exhibit extreme and erratic slowdowns: a sudden plan switch to a full-table scan or wide nested loop holds many row or page locks for far longer than usual, magnifying lock-wait times, deadlock frequency, and application time-outs. Sessions that pile up behind the blockers spawn additional server processes or threads until the operating-system quota for PIDs, file descriptors, or semaphore sets is reached, after which new connections, background workers, or parallel query helpers fail to start. Operators may observe a mixture of symptoms—escalating lock-wait graphs, deadlock-victim errors, optimizer plan regressions in execution-plan caches, and kernel log messages about "too many open files" or "cannot allocate memory"—making root-cause isolation difficult.

Causal chain: a poor plan (1) dramatically lengthens critical sections, enlarging the time windows in which locks are held; (2) the prolonged locks throttle other transactions, causing them to queue and accumulate; (3) each waiting or retrying session consumes additional database back-end processes, file descriptors, and shared-memory objects; (4) once kernel limits are saturated, even diagnostic queries or deadlock-detector threads may fail to start, further delaying lock resolution and forcing the engine into partial outage. The three anomalies therefore reinforce one another—sub-optimal planning triggers lock storms, which in turn drive the system to exhaust OS resources, amplifying the performance collapse and complicating recovery.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle within an open transaction for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle, waiting for a client query, while an open transaction remains active longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; this prevents long idle transactions from holding locks or preventing vacuum cleanup.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
